2610.16256.abstract: Head-mounted body and bimanual motion capture supports self-avatars, teleoperation, and embodied demonstrations. However, a single egocentric camera is vulnerable to a limited field of view, scale ambiguity, and hand-object occlusion. We present EgoWholeView, a wearable capture system of six synchronized wide-angle RGB cameras with a role-specialized pipeline. The outward views localize the rig in a world frame, while an overlapping downward pair independently predicts SMPL-X body and MANO hand parameters. Both predictors are adapted to egocentric fisheye data. To combine the two, reliability cues measured from the predictions themselves weight the fusion of body and hand joint rotations, while shape is aggregated across views and frames. The pair's baseline fixes metric scale, and triangulation recovers root translation. Relative to monocular prediction, fusion reduces PA-MPJPE by 3.7% for the body and 11.2% for the hands, and temporal refinement lowers angular-acceleration magnitude by 32.2% and 31.0%, respectively. On our six-camera recording, the pipeline produces body and hand states in a shared world frame using benchmark-fitted gates without retuning, and temporal refinement lowers hand acceleration magnitude by 41.08%. Using only RGB cameras and no third-person view, EgoWholeView offers a low-cost, portable route to egocentric interaction data.

2610.16272.title: Graph3R: Unifying View Graph Initialization with Feed-Forward Reconstruction
2610.16272.abstract: Feed-forward reconstruction recovers camera poses and dense geometry from image sets whose views are assumed to come from a single scene. In practice, uncurated image collections often contain views from disjoint scenes, and reconstructing these views jointly can corrupt camera poses and geometry. Existing pipelines typically resolve view associations in separate stages before final reconstruction, leaving view graph initialization and reconstruction inference only loosely coupled. We introduce Graph3R, which unifies view graph initialization with feed-forward reconstruction through a shared geometric representation. A lightweight verification head predicts pairwise covisibility from the multi-view features of $\pi^3$ to construct a view graph. This graph classifies the input views into scene groups. For each group, we mask the shared features before decoding camera poses and dense geometry. Reusing the multi-view features allows Graph3R to reconstruct disjoint scenes separately with a single backbone pass. Across three benchmarks, Graph3R improves average maximum recall at 100% precision by upto 8.99 percentage points over the baseline, while improving reconstruction quality on mixed-scene inputs. Regarding the multi-session mapping task, Graph3R improves cross-session localization and achieves competitive pose estimation accuracy, while delivering a runtime speedup of approximately $35.9\times$ over the baseline when reconstructing the query group. By integrating learned view association with geometric inference, our approach takes a step toward end-to-end reconstruction from uncurated image collections.

2610.16277.title: FlowAvatar: Real-Time Full-Body Avatars from Sparse Egocentric Inputs on Consumer XR Devices
2610.16277.abstract: Prior avatar embodiment research has studied tracking completeness (how faithfully the body, hands, and face are sensed and reproduced) and personalized appearance in isolation, each requiring specialized lab equipment. How these factors interact on consumer hardware remains an open question, because no existing system unifies body pose, face, hands, and personalized appearance on a standalone headset. We present FlowAvatar, a system enabling real-time personalized look-alike avatars with full-body pose, hand articulation, facial expression, and eye gaze tracking from sparse egocentric inputs on consumer XR devices (Meta Quest Pro). Our pose model achieves competitive spatial accuracy and state-of-the-art temporal consistency on the AMASS benchmark against prior works with comprehensive spatial and temporal losses validated through architecture and loss ablations, while running in real-time. Two user studies (N=12, N=10) provide converging evidence that tracking completeness and personalized appearance serve complementary roles: tracking completeness broadly improves perceived motion quality, while only their combination achieves positive total embodiment.

2610.16278.title: DepthTile: Depth-Guided Existing-Image Self-Tiling with Input-Side Tileability Assessment
2610.16278.abstract: Existing-image self-tiling aims to transform a given image into a seamlessly repeatable tile while preserving its original semantics and local details. This task requires weak editing to retain the source but leave periodic seams, whereas strong editing improves tileability at the large risk of content this http URL diffusion-based tiling pipelines alleviate boundary discontinuities, yet lack awareness of which regions are geometrically important to preserve. In this work, we propose DepthTile, a depth-guided self-tiling method whose generation module requires no retraining of the diffusion backbone. It converts monocular depth into a spatial preservation prior and integrates it into the timestep-dependent masking mechanism of Tiled Diffusion. DepthTile converts depth into a spatial editability map and fuses it with the differential diffusion mask. This strengthens source preservation in near-field regions indicated by the monocular depth prior while retaining editing flexibility near compatible background boundaries. To access when self-tiling is feasible, we introduce the Self-Tiling Ability Score (STAS), a lightweight input-side predictor based on RGB, gradient, depth, and depth-gradient cues. On a 335-image benchmark, relative to the default Tiled Diffusion pipeline, DepthTile reduces MAE, LPIPS, and Tiling Score by 12.8%, 26.7%, and 8.4%, respectively. STAS reliably enables difficulty-aware analysis and further supports compatibility-aware pairwise image tiling.

2610.16292.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Fine-grained Urban Scene Reconstruction via Semantic-guided Density Control and Loss Design
2610.16292.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has been becoming a promising 3D reconstruction technique because of its advantage of high-fidelity rendering effect with high efficiency. However, it still suffers from coarse density control and semantically blind loss functions when reconstructing the fine-grained structures in complex urban scenes. Thus, this study proposes SG-GS, a semantic-guided 3DGS method for fine-grained structure reconstruction. It takes the semantic segmentation deduced by the Segment Anything Model (SAM) as a constraint and systematically integrates it into both Gaussian density control and loss function design. On the one hand, a semantic-constrained adaptive density control mechanism is constructed, which dynamically allocates gradient thresholds to different semantic regions of the scene and introduces an additional boundary-enhanced densification strategy, so that new Gaussians are directed to structurally critical regions. On the other hand, a multi-feature guided loss function is designed, and fine-grained supervision signals are gradually introduced through a phased progressive training strategy, alleviating the artifacts caused by the lack of semantic constraints in the basic loss. Experiments on three datasets show that the proposed method consistently improves reconstruction accuracy. Compared with the original 3DGS, the PSNR increases by approximately 2.7% to 5.2%, while artifacts on linear structures and boundary blurring are effectively mitigated. The method can serve the fine-grained 3D reconstruction of urban scenes.

2610.16293.title: ClothAtlas: Joint Garment Identification and State Estimation under Self-Occlusion
2610.16293.abstract: Garment manipulation requires inferring both garment identity and complete configuration from partial, self-occluded observations. This creates a chicken-and-egg problem: completing a partial observation requires a garment-specific deformation prior, while identifying the garment requires a configuration that explains the observation. We introduce ClothAtlas, which jointly identifies garments and estimates their complete configurations from partial point clouds and a library of canonical meshes. A shared graph-conditioned flow-matching model samples configurations for each candidate mesh and ranks candidates by observation fit. The model accommodates different mesh shapes, vertex counts, and connectivities, allowing new garments to be added from canonical meshes alone without retraining. On held-out DexGarmentLab garments, ClothAtlas ranks the correct mesh first among 221 candidates for all 22 test garments from a single flat observation. From a single self-occluded observation, it identifies 15/22 garments, compared with 8/22 for a deterministic graph estimator. Persistent vertex identities support grasp-target localization on real garments, reducing mean error from 15.4 to 6.4 cm overall and from 17.0 to 8.3 cm on occluded targets compared with dense descriptor matching. Project page: this https URL

2610.16299.title: Learning Temporal Evidence Selection for Video Anomaly Understanding
2610.16299.abstract: Video anomaly understanding (VAU) aims to generate language-level interpretations of anomalous events in long videos, requiring visual evidence that supports explanation beyond anomaly detection alone. Existing VAU pipelines commonly rely on anomaly-centric or predefined temporal sampling strategies, which efficiently emphasize suspicious moments but overlook contextual cues, object interactions, and temporally distributed evidence needed for reasoning. Motivated by recent progress in learnable temporal selection for long-video question answering, we revisit VAU temporal sampling as a downstream-aligned evidence selection problem. We introduce the semantic-conditioned Temporal Sampling Q-Former that learns to select temporal visual evidence through the VAU generation objective. Since generic VAU prompts provide weak video-specific guidance, we condition the sampler on CLIP-embedded object tags automatically extracted from the input video. These tags are used only for temporal evidence selection and are not appended to the LLM generation prompt, separating sampler conditioning from prompt augmentation. The proposed sampler operates in visual-token space, computes soft temporal selection weights from frame-level representations, and merges duplicated selections before response generation. Experiments on HIVAU-70K show that our model achieves the best performance among the compared fine-tuned models, while ablations demonstrate that learnable temporal sampling improves over fixed anomaly-focused sampling and that CLIP-embedded object-tag conditioning further improves over generic-prompt conditioning. Our results suggest that temporal sampling in VAU should be aligned with explanation-oriented evidence utility rather than anomaly saliency alone.

2610.16320.title: Building age estimation based on widely available multi-source1 geospatial data
2610.16320.abstract: Building age is fundamental for urban infrastructure safety, operation, and planning, as it directly affects structural safety, and sustainable development. Existing methods mostly rely on detailed building information such as street view, function, or materials, which are harder to obtain than geospatial data like satellite imagery and Digital Surface Models (DSMs). However, existing methods based on those geospatial data mainly rely on optical imagery and local texture features, limiting their ability to capture structural information and distinguish buildings from different periods. Moreover, the inherent temporal ordering among building age categories is often overlooked. To address these limitations, we propose the first deep-learning framework for multi-building age estimation using widely available multi-source geospatial data, including remote sensing data and their derived products, as well as building footprint information that estimates age at both pixel and instance levels within a unified pipeline. Specifically, a large pretrained backbone with fine-tuning adapters extracts representative features, and raster-derived and property-derived fusion modules support pixel-wise and instance-wise predictions. Pixel-level estimation employs a pyramid decoder with Cosine-guided Mixture-of-Experts (CMoE) to fuse multi-source raster data across scales, capturing fine-grained building age differences, while instance-level prediction uses attention pooling and Property-Conditional Adaptive Instance Normalization (PCAdaIN) to extract instance-level representations and integrate property attributes. A Temporal Ordinal Constraint Loss (TOCL) enforces the sequential ordering of predicted ages. We also construct a building age benchmark for Hong Kong to enable comprehensive evaluation. The source code and datasets are available at this https URL.

2610.16324.title: Anomaly-Guided Observation and Two-Level Semantic Feedback for Training-Free Video Anomaly Analysis
2610.16324.abstract: Training-free language-based video anomaly detection (VAD) uses frozen vision--language models (VLMs) and large language models (LLMs) to localize abnormal events without task-specific model-weight optimization. Existing approaches increasingly exploit broader temporal and semantic context, yet generic context does not necessarily foreground abnormal events or specify how video-level semantics should modify local anomaly scores. We introduce a training-free semantic feedback framework that uses VAD-guided active observation for video anomaly understanding (VAU) and returns the resulting anomaly-focused description to refine temporal detection. Starting from an upstream anomaly-score curve, we adapt reasoning-based iterative frame selection: high-score regions seed the observations, and anomaly scores together with VLM relevance assessments guide subsequent temporal exploration. A frozen video-language model generates a single open-ended anomaly description from the selected frames. The description is returned through two complementary feedback levels: video-level feedback determines whether the score distribution should be suppressed, preserved, or sharpened, with selective visual rechecking, while local feedback retrieves event-related windows and promotes scores only after target-local visual verification. All model weights remain frozen, and feedback is applied once without regenerating the description. On the HIVAU video-summary evaluations of UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, VAD-guided observation improves GPT-rated reasonability, detail, and consistency over the matched CLIP-guided variant. For VAD, semantic feedback improves the re-evaluated upstream detector from 84.36% to 86.25% AUC on UCF-Crime and from 68.07% to 72.58% AP on XD-Violence, where the final AUC is 91.74%.

2610.16329.title: Explicitly Aligned Multi-View Breast Cancer Risk Prediction from Variable-Length Screening Histories
2610.16329.abstract: Accurate breast cancer risk prediction from screening mammography is essential for improved risk stratification and personalized screening. It can benefit from both temporal breast tissue changes across longitudinal examinations and complementary anatomical information from craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views. Leveraging longitudinal information requires identifying corresponding tissue regions across examinations, yet most approaches rely on implicit feature alignment without explicitly enforcing spatial consistency. Recent work has demonstrated the benefits of explicit temporal alignment; however, existing methods model each view independently, preventing them from exploiting complementary CC and MLO information. Furthermore, explicit approaches have been limited to a single prior examination. To fill these gaps, we propose (this http URL), a breast-wise longitudinal multi-view framework that jointly models CC and MLO views across screening examinations while accommodating a variable number of prior examinations. FlexLMV-Net explicitly aligns longitudinal feature maps and integrates complementary views through cross-view temporal fusion and a dual-stream attention block. Evaluated on EMBED and CSAW-CC, FlexLMV-Net consistently outperforms existing approaches across breast density, cancer subtypes, and demographic subgroups, highlighting the benefits of explicit longitudinal alignment, multi-view modeling, and flexible use of available screening history. We further introduce (this http URL), an open-source benchmark that unifies state-of-the-art single- and multi-timepoint breast cancer risk prediction models under standardized preprocessing, training, inference, and evaluation protocols, enabling fair and reproducible comparison of existing methods.

2610.16330.title: BAT3R: Robust Online 3D Reconstruction with Bayesian Adaptive State Updates
2610.16330.abstract: Feed-forward transformer models have driven remarkable progress in 3D vision,yet their quadratic complexity renders them impractical for long video sequences. Streaming 3D reconstruction addresses this bottleneck by processing frames sequen?tially with constant memory. However, existing recurrent architectures inevitably suffer from progressive degradation over long sequences, as they fail to account for the intrinsic reliability of observations and the accumulated confidence of the historical state, leading to severe error accumulation. To address these issues, we introduce BAT3R, a training-free Bayesian adaptation framework comprising two synergistic modules: State Innovation Gating (SIG) and Bayesian-guided Adaptive State Updating (BASU). SIG acts as a distributional regularizer that anchors state evolution to its geometric initialization, effectively arresting representational drift during long-term inference. Building on this, BASU reformulates state update as a recursive Bayesian inference process within a Kalman filtering framework. By jointly modeling the temporal reliability of observations via information-theoretic gain and spatial relevance via cross-attention maps, BASU achieves an asymmetric spatio-temporal state fusion: well-consolidated historical regions are protected from redundant updates, while genuinely novel scene content is aggressively incor?porated. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks (7-Scenes, TUM, ScanNet, KITTI, etc.) demonstrate that BAT3R consistently outperforms state-of-the-art online 3D reconstruction methods, with the most significant gains observed on long sequences and complex scenes.

2610.16337.title: WorldRoPE: Probabilistic World-Centric Rotary Embedding for Multi-View Attention
2610.16337.abstract: Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE) is widely used to encode relative positions in Transformers. In multi-view settings, however, patch coordinates are defined independently in each image: the same 3D point can therefore have different coordinates across views, making them insufficient for establishing cross-view correspondences. We introduce WorldRoPE, a probabilistic world-centric RoPE for multi-view attention. At each layer, WorldRoPE back-projects each patch token into a set of volumetric Gaussian primitives in a shared world frame. These primitives represent multiple plausible 3D supports for a token, jointly capturing alternative depth hypotheses, depth uncertainty, and the finite spatial extent of its patch frustum. When a key token's support is projected into a query view, it induces a distribution over where that key may appear in the query image. WorldRoPE integrates the rotary operator over this distribution in closed form, combining rotations at the projected primitive centers according to their mixture weights with covariance-dependent attenuation. This makes attention less sensitive to uncertain key locations in the query view, without rasterizing or warping token features. The formulation reduces to deterministic RoPE when the support collapses to a point. Across layers, the predicted geometry guides cross-view attention, while the updated features refine the geometry used at the next layer. Experiments on novel view synthesis, depth estimation, and 3D geometry reconstruction demonstrate the effectiveness of WorldRoPE for multi-view Transformers.

2610.16338.title: SyncReward: Human-Aligned Synchronization Reward for Audio-Visual Generation
2610.16338.abstract: Recent years have witnessed rapid progress in joint audio--visual generation. However, audio--visual synchronization remains a challenge, as generated speech and sound often temporally misalign with visual events. A key bottleneck is the lack of human-annotated data, reliable evaluation benchmarks, and synchronization-aware evaluation models for generated audio--visual outputs. To address these limitations, we conduct a comprehensive study spanning data, benchmarking, and reward modeling. We first introduce SyncReward-Data-80K, a dataset containing 80K professional synchronization ratings for clips from eight audio--visual generators. A taxonomy-guided construction pipeline covers four sound-event families: Speech, Onset, Instrument, and Ambient. We further construct \textbf{SyncReward-Bench}, a held-out benchmark of 1K clips, each independently rated by multiple professionals. Using this benchmark, we systematically evaluate specialized synchronization metrics and omni-modal models, revealing their substantial misalignment with human judgments. Finally, we develop SyncReward, a reward model that combines semantic--temporal contrastive pretraining on real clips with human supervision on generated clips. As an evaluation metric, SyncReward achieves the strongest agreement with human ratings among the evaluated methods. As a reward, it improves synchronization through inference-time best-of-$N$ selection and reinforcement learning based post-training. We will release the data, benchmark, model, and code at this https URL.

2610.16357.title: VideoSlate: Stateful Commit Control for Temporally Grounded Agentic Video Reasoning
2610.16357.abstract: Agentic video reasoning systems gather and assess video evidence across stages, selecting relevant spans as visual evidence for answering questions. New candidates and observations prompt reassessment of the current span, but revisions can correct localization errors or discard useful evidence already present in the adopted span. Systems therefore need to connect evidence organization across stages with temporal state control, allowing accumulated information to jointly inform revision assessment while explicit adoption decisions govern how assessment outcomes affect downstream visual evidence. We introduce VideoSlate, a stateful commit-control framework built around shared evidence. A typed evidence blackboard links candidate spans, provenance, construction, and verifier observations, enabling an incumbent-relative certifier to assess revision support from the candidate, current span, and related proposals. Based on certification, the controller authorizes a revision or retains the current span, separating evidence accumulation from state updates and recording each decision and its evidence on the blackboard. Extensive evaluations across video grounding and grounded question-answering benchmarks show that VideoSlate can improve temporal localization through selective revision.

2610.16364.title: From Sound to Sense: An Anatomy of Semantic Supervision for Speech-Driven Visual Grounding in Remote Sensing Imagery
2610.16364.abstract: Speech-driven visual grounding in remote sensing (RSVG) removes the typing bottleneck of text-based interaction and is intended to preserve prosodic intent, enabling hands-free target acquisition in time-critical missions. The direct-audio paradigm, mapping raw speech straight to a bounding box and bypassing automatic speech recognition (ASR), was recently adopted by RSTalker, but what such grounders actually learn about language remains unmeasured. SemEcho grafts a frozen Whisper speech pathway onto a VLTVG grounding host so that speech and text share one decoder, making the paired text, free by construction since speech corpora in this task are synthesized from DIOR-RSVG expressions, a training-time teacher and a fair, same-host text upper bound. On this instrument we dissect three semantic injection channels (feature-mimicry distillation, word-level CTC supervision, and two-stage ASR pretraining) with linear semantic probes, and release Audio-DIOR-R (80,973 training clips; 10 timbres x K=3; Qwen3-TTS synthesis with online sox noise lambda in [0, 0.4]) and Audio-DIOR-Comp, a re-split holding out 17 attribute-category combinations under a 2x2 acoustic-semantic protocol. Our anatomy yields four findings. (i) Whether direct alignment beats a domain-trained ASR cascade is decided by recognizer quality: against a weak in-domain cascade (CTC 0.53) direct wins by 9.0 Acc@0.5 points with transcription errors concentrated on spatial-relation words, but a strong in-domain cascade (CTC 0.029) reaches the text upper bound (80.8 vs. 81.0) and beats even the strongest direct model by 8.8 points; the anti-ASR premise holds only against weak recognizers.

2610.16383.title: Throwing4: Phase-Aware Pose Modeling for Throw-Distance Prediction in Elite Athletics
2610.16383.abstract: Elite athletics throwing provides a structured biomechanical action sequence together with an objective continuous outcome, namely throw distance, making it a suitable setting for performance-oriented sports analytics. In this work, we investigate whether explicit phase alignment of pose dynamics improves throw-distance prediction under realistic broadcast conditions. To support this study, we curate Throwing4, a dataset of 500 elite throwing clips spanning javelin, discus, hammer, and shot put, with corresponding two-dimensional pose sequences, frame-level phase annotations, and official distance labels. We formulate throw-distance prediction from broadcast-derived pose as a regression problem and compare full-sequence modeling against a phase-conditioned approach that partitions each attempt into four technique stages and fuses phase-specific motion representations. Experiments across multiple graph-based pose encoders show a consistent reduction in prediction error when phase structure is incorporated, indicating that phase-aligned modeling provides a more stable representation than treating the entire motion as an unstructured sequence. These findings suggest that explicit biomechanical phase information is a useful inductive prior for pose-based performance modeling in elite athletics throwing. Beyond score prediction, the dataset and protocol provide a basis for future work on fine-grained technique analysis, interpretable sports analytics, and robust modeling from broadcast video.

2610.16409.title: Recovering from Pose-Selection Failures in Repeated Visual Localization
2610.16409.abstract: Repetitive structures can give an incorrect pose candidate more inlier support than an accurate one, causing visual localization to select it. History-Guided Pose Reselection (HPR) uses coarse position forecasts from up to five past localization outputs to distinguish well-separated current-query candidates. The best-fitting forecast proposes an alternative; HPR accepts it only if every well-fitting forecast is much closer to it than to the localizer's pose. HPR needs no odometry and returns the selected candidate unchanged, using prediction for selection rather than pose refinement. With one development-set threshold, HPR improves recall within 5 meters and 10 degrees in all 12 main configurations of Hierarchical Localization (HLoc), MASt3R-based pose generation, and JIST-based retrieval, losing successes on fewer than 0.4 percent of queries. On NAVER Gangnam B1, HPR corrects 97 HLoc failures and loses six successes; gains persist within 0.25 meters and 2 degrees on all three HLoc test sets. Median HPR runtime on HLoc candidates is below one millisecond, excluding pose generation. Recovery weakens under less frequent localization.

2610.16417.title: Not All Challenges Are Equal: Evaluating Interactive Liveness Detection Against Real-Time Face Swaps
2610.16417.abstract: Remote identity verification assumes that a camera stream shows a live person, yet public real-time face-swap tools can replace that person before the stream reaches the verifier. Passive deepfake detectors generalize poorly to new generators, while interactive challenges are often selected without evidence of which gestures expose current attacks. We evaluate randomized gesture challenges in 108 live sessions with six subjects, 24 impersonated identities, and two face-swap tools, DeepFaceLive and FaceFusion, injected through a virtual camera. The static calibration segment reaches a session-level AUC of 0.878 with a frozen UCF spatial detector, while the mean across the active-gesture windows reaches 0.988. Pose and combined gestures have the highest point estimates, whereas expressions show no clear improvement. Hand occlusion against FaceFusion, configured with an occlusion mask, scores below the static baseline. The end-to-end time required to satisfy the validator also distinguishes attacks from genuine sessions, achieving a session-level AUC of 0.732, although this signal includes synthesis and transport delays. These results show that challenge sets should be tested against current attack configurations and that response time can provide an additional, deployment-specific signal.

2610.16441.title: VisExMEM: Visual Evidence-Based Explainable Multimodal Evaluation Metric
2610.16441.abstract: Current image-text evaluation often relies on a global score, which gives limited insight into which semantic details are supported by the image. Explainable metrics provide rationales, but the visual evidence supporting those rationales can still be difficult to verify. We introduce VisExMEM, a reference-free evaluator that decomposes captions into atomic claims, localizes visual evidence, verifies each claim, and averages claim-level support into a global score. Explanations use the same evidence and decisions. We train Qwen3.5-based 4B and 9B models on 100K samples with multi-task SFT, counterfactual refinement, and evidence-aware GDPO. Across eight benchmarks, VisExMEM-9B achieves the highest descriptive composite among open-source evaluators in our comparison, exceeding VQAScore by 11.7 points while remaining competitive with GPT-5.6 Sol. We also introduce AGITA-Bench, containing 600 human-annotated image-text pairs and 8.7K atomic claims for global and claim-level evaluation. For untuned Qwen3.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol controls, decomposed prompting raises the same composite by 3.6-5.1 points relative to holistic prompting. Human evaluation shows that VisExMEM explanations outperform prior explainable metrics and approach GPT-5.6 Sol.

2610.16444.title: Pixels or Code? Benchmarking Instruction-Guided Visual Artifact Operation
2610.16444.abstract: Visual artifacts such as charts, technical diagrams, webpages, and document pages underpin scientific, commercial, and engineering workflows. Editing these artifacts requires direct modification, dependency-aware updates, preservation of unaffected content, and compliance with domain constraints. We define this capability as Visual Artifact Operation (VAO). Prior benchmarks test parts of this problem, including cascading updates in charts. We study direct edits, dependent updates, and preservation across visual domains and pixel, code, and agent paradigms under one image-only protocol. We introduce Visual Artifact Operation Bench (VAO-Bench), comprising 1,573 manually screened tasks across nine artifact categories and three difficulty levels. VAO-Bench uses executable artifacts and deterministic rendering to trace reference transformations and annotate direct edits, dependent updates, and preservation constraints. All systems receive the same source image and instruction; we evaluate pixel-space editors, code-generating multimodal systems, and tool-using agents on direct-edit accuracy, dependency-aware update, content preservation, domain validity, and visual quality. Experiments show that executable-code systems better support dependent updates, while pixel-space editors offer faster execution and strong visual quality. Explicitly stating dependencies improves both paradigms, identifying implicit-update inference as a central bottleneck. VAO-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for dependable visual artifact editing across generation paradigms.

2610.16448.title: Tikhonov-Stabilized Bezier Representation Forecasting for Training-free Diffusion Acceleration
2610.16448.abstract: Diffusion models, particularly Diffusion Transformers, achieve strong image and video generation quality but remain expensive at inference time due to repeated denoiser evaluations. Feature caching offers a deployment-friendly acceleration strategy by reusing or predicting intermediate representations without retraining the generator or modifying the sampler. However, existing cache-then-forecast methods often rely on Taylor-style finite-difference extrapolation, which can become unstable over longer cache intervals, and typically predict local module outputs whose errors may accumulate through subsequent denoiser blocks. We propose \textbf{BeziCast}, a training-free diffusion acceleration framework that forecasts output-proximal denoising representations using low-order B'ezier trajectories. BeziCast estimates B'ezier control points via Tikhonov-stabilized fitting, providing a smooth, capacity-controlled temporal parameterization that avoids explicit high-order derivative estimation and decouples trajectory capacity from cache-query density. To moderate aggressive extrapolation, we further derive equivalent forecasting weights and introduce a convex-hull-inspired guardrail that detects high-risk predictions and softly pulls them toward a conservative simplex-projected estimate. Extensive evaluations across advanced image and video diffusion models demonstrate the effectiveness of BeziCast. In particular, BeziCast accelerates FLUX.1 by up to (4.79\times) and HunyuanVideo by up to (4.11\times), while preserving substantially better generation quality than competing acceleration baselines.

2610.16452.title: Not Every Cue Is Evidence: Cue Supportability for Forensic Distillation in Face Forgery Detection
2610.16452.abstract: Explainable face forgery detection requires not only correct judgments but also forensic evidence supported by the input image. However, training cues are typically derived from the forgery generation pipeline. Since images available to the model are of limited quality and resolution, it is difficult to observe the fine-grained traces these cues refer to. Training methods that further supply such cues as privileged supervision exacerbate the problem, as the student is taught to articulate evidence it cannot perceive. The student consequently resorts to templated or over-generalized expressions, giving rise to the correct-answer, wrong-evidence (CAWE) failure. We propose a dual supportability audit that filters privileged cues before distillation. Each candidate cue must be predictable from the remaining privileged context and causally tied to high-attribution visual regions in the current image. Only cues satisfying both conditions receive substantial distillation weight, preventing unsupported details from leaking into the student. Experiments across eight benchmarks show that our method maintains or improves detection accuracy while significantly raising explanation faithfulness compared to existing paradigms.

2610.16455.title: GHOST: Geometry-Constrained Hybrid Diffusion for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation
2610.16455.abstract: 3D scene graph generation requires understanding both object semantics and metric spatial relations. However, existing open-vocabulary methods often struggle with spatial predicates because language similarity reflects semantic co-occurrence rather than explicit geometry. We propose GHOST, a Geometry-constrained Hybrid diffusion framework for Open-vocabulary 3D Scene graph generaTion. GHOST jointly models continuous node geometry and discrete edge predicates, following a geometry-to-constraint-to-predicate denoising process to ensure geometrically consistent relation prediction. It introduces language-grounded constraint induction, which maps predicate embeddings to differentiable geometric constraints that guide both layout refinement and predicate reweighting. A Geometry-Topology Collaborative Denoiser further couples node and edge reasoning through noise-adaptive interaction and orientation-aware modeling. Experiments on 3DSSG demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both closed-set and open-vocabulary settings, including over 17-point gains over RelationField on spatial predicates.

2610.16465.title: Teaching Vision-Language Models to Decline: Support Completion Against Mirage
2610.16465.abstract: Vision-language models answer questions about images they were never shown, a failure called mirage. Such an answer can be correct without being justified by the evidence, and the difference matters wherever a model's output is checked by someone who did not see its input. We locate the failure in the training objective: cross-entropy separates a model that reads the image from one that ignores it by only the conditional mutual information between answer and image, and no training example rewards declining. We formalise support completion, TIDE, which also shows each training question with a blank image, a same-domain wrong image and an out-of-domain image, with targets that decline, and prove that under TIDE every image-blind predictor is suboptimal by at least 1.04 nats per example, that the optimum declines exactly on the counterfactual kinds while keeping its behaviour on valid images, and that for any finite model the error of its answer-or-decline decision, declining on valid input plus answering on invalid input, is bounded below by how well its representation separates valid from invalid evidence. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B under a frozen held-out protocol with two judges, the three-condition predecessor of TIDE reduced the invalid-evidence mirage rate from 0.759 to 0.097 and the blank-image rate from 0.700 to 0.003 at a false-abstention cost of 0.126; label-free grounding raised the rate to 0.859, a likelihood-advantage contrast moved it only to 0.718 because its empty-image term carries no gradient, and grounding applied after support completion re-opened the mirage. The four-condition protocol on three base models, with seeds and component ablations, is in progress and not reported here.

2610.16471.title: Auditing Observation-Quality Shortcuts in the Evaluation of Person-Centered Motion for Video Anomaly Detection
2610.16471.abstract: Video anomaly detection (VAD) identifies deviations from normal patterns, but such deviations do not necessarily correspond to safety-critical events. We focus on human-centered emergencies and violence and investigate whether motion-based anomaly discrimination reflects task-relevant motion information or observation-quality differences arising from person detection, pose estimation, and tracking. We introduce an observation-quality-aware evaluation framework that combines quality diagnostics, quality balancing, motion orthogonalization, and robustness analyses. On human-centered categories of UCF-Crime, quality-only features match or exceed the discrimination of multi-cue motion in the original cohort, revealing a strong observation-quality shortcut. After cardinality matching brings all 11 measured quality variables below a prespecified marginal balance threshold, multi-cue motion consistently outperforms quality-only features across Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and RBF-SVM, yielding ROC-AUC gains of 0.046-0.141. Because nonlinear quality-only prediction remains above chance after matching, we interpret this result as additional discrimination beyond measured marginal quality rather than as evidence of quality-free or causal motion understanding. These findings show that high VAD performance should not be interpreted as evidence of abnormal-motion modeling without auditing the reliability of the person-observation pipeline. Our study provides a systematic protocol for evaluating observation-quality shortcuts and for assessing whether motion-based discrimination survives explicit control of detection, pose-estimation, and tracking reliability.

2610.16482.title: MiMaAlign: Hierarchical Micro-Macro Alignment for Physically Plausible Video Generation
2610.16482.abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models have made remarkable progress in generating high-fidelity visuals, yet their outputs still often exhibit physically implausible phenomena, including discontinuous dynamics and implausible event interactions. Existing representation alignment methods mainly transfer generic video features or short-range motion cues, treating physical plausibility as a single-level representation problem. To address this issue, we propose MiMaAlign, a hierarchical micro-macro alignment framework that transfers complementary dynamics-oriented and event-oriented knowledge into different abstraction depths of a pretrained video diffusion model. Specifically, micro-level continuous dynamics alignment imposes constraints by aligning diffusion features with a continuous-time motion representation learned by a Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (Neural ODE), while macro-level event-commonsense alignment provides representations of object interactions and event semantics through an instruction-prompted vision-language model (VLM). With training-only auxiliary objectives, we align the complementary supervision from the two teachers with shallower and deeper generator features, respectively, enabling the generator to internalize the corresponding physical priors. Empirical evaluations show that, on CogVideoX-2B, MiMaAlign achieves a relative improvement of up to 21.0% in the Physical Commonsense (PC) score on the VideoPhy benchmark over the baseline, and also delivers substantial gains on the highly challenging VideoPhy2 benchmark, while maintaining general video quality on VBench and being supported by blind user comparisons.

2610.16500.title: Self-Verifier Capture in Unified Visual Generators: Diagnosing and Repairing Closed-Loop Self-Reward
2610.16500.abstract: Image-space reward requires decoding and a separate judge; unified visual generators can instead reuse their understanding pathway for decode-free, self-supplied reward. Optimizing against this verifier closes the self-reward loop; shared trainable weights let one update move generation and scoring even with the reward gradient stopped. We call the resulting failure self-verifier capture: self-reward rises while independently measured quality falls. Matched semantic/denoising by shared/frozen cells on Scale-RAE isolate two routes: the policy exploits on-manifold blind spots of a frozen semantic judge, while shared updates additionally rewrite the judge. A frozen judge also becomes stale, and repeated self-refresh yields progressively weaker recoveries. The diagnosis yields a two-part repair: locking the warmed reward read blocks rewriting, while sparse, parameter-disjoint external anchors counter residual exploitation. Unanchored rollouts retain semantic reward across multiple latent noise levels, providing dense latent reward that terminal image-space judging cannot supply, while a drift-triggered controller allocates anchors to high-drift rollouts and propagates their calibration within each group. At matched budgets, the controller improves on fixed-dose anchoring, increasingly so as coverage tightens. Both the unanchored failure and the repair transfer to the higher-performing, architecturally distinct Show-o2. Across both bases, the complete method significantly outperforms a construct-matched every-rollout judge on GenEval and DPG-Bench while externally scoring only 1/16 of rollouts. At 1/32 coverage, it scores higher in all four comparisons and remains jointly non-inferior.

2610.16502.title: KARAMEL: Knowledge-Aware Ranking for Multimodal Entity Linking in the Arts via Heterogeneous Graphs
2610.16502.abstract: Discovering and disambiguating entities from multimodal and heterogeneous data is a key challenge in discovery science, where relevant knowledge is often implicit and distributed across modalities. We present KARAMEL, a framework for multimodal entity linking (MEL) - the task of aligning visual and textual mentions to entities in a knowledge base - in the cultural heritage domain. Unlike prior vision-language models that primarily rely on surface-level multimodal alignment, our approach incorporates sociohistorical and contextual knowledge through a knowledge-aware architecture that fuses a vision-language encoder with a heterogeneous graph neural network. This design enables contextual reasoning over complex relational structures and supports robust entity disambiguation under ambiguous or underspecified evidence. To benchmark multimodal discovery in this setting, we introduce WikiMuSA (Wikidata-based Multimodal Semantic data for Art), a new dataset that links artworks to Wikidata entities via images, textual descriptions, and structured contextual knowledge. Experimental results show that KARAMEL surpasses strong baselines, particularly on implicit or abstract mentions, while ablation studies highlight the critical role of domain-specific, structured context in learning expressive representations. While instantiated in the cultural heritage domain, KARAMEL addresses a general knowledge discovery problem and applies to other scientific settings involving multimodal observations and heterogeneous background knowledge. Both the dataset and source code are made publicly available.

2610.16529.title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
2610.16529.abstract: Plant fibers are increasingly used as sustainable reinforcements in composites, but the intrinsic variability of their microstructure causes substantial scatter in transverse mechanical behavior, complicating composite design. Characterizing this behavior relies on finite element (FE) simulations requiring several minutes of high-performance computing per fiber, making high-throughput characterization across realistic fiber populations impractical. In this study, we propose a deep learning framework replacing this FE bottleneck with a fast pipeline. It includes two coupled recursive U-Nets predicting the step-by-step evolution of fiber deformation and internal stress fields under transverse compression, followed by a regression CNN estimating the transverse Young's modulus from the final stress field. Unlike prior approaches predicting stress fields for fixed configurations or idealized geometries, our framework recursively resolves the full temporal stress evolution for synthetic fibers derived from real hemp cross-sections, with or without a lumen. Trained on 1,000 synthetic fiber geometries with FE ground truth, it reproduces the stress field sequence with a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of $0.9574 \pm 0.0074$ and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of $0.0345 \pm 0.0079$. It estimates transverse Young's modulus with an $R^2$ of $0.938 \pm 0.024$, a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of $24.31 \pm 1.23$ MPa, and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of $5.25 \pm 0.91\%$. Inference requires under one second per fiber versus five minutes per FE simulation, drastically reducing computational cost. This offers a fast, reliable tool for mechanical characterization of synthetic plant fibers, with promising applications in designing natural fiber-reinforced composites.

2610.16545.title: Heuristics are Not Enough: Calibrated and Corrected Caching for Video Diffusion Acceleration
2610.16545.abstract: Feature caching has become a mainstream training-free strategy for accelerating video diffusion models by reusing intermediate outputs across denoising steps. However, existing adaptive methods rely on heuristic difference measures misaligned with actual generation quality, employ a single global threshold that ignores heterogeneous phase dynamics, and never validate their budget estimates against true approximation error, allowing systematic bias to propagate uncorrected. We propose \textbf{AlignCache}, a closed-loop caching framework that directly aligns scheduling decisions with their true influence on the final generated video through three tightly coupled components: (1) phase-adaptive budget routing that partitions the denoising trajectory into structurally distinct phases, each governed by an independent threshold and a staleness-aware guard; (2) closed-loop threshold calibration that exploits counterfactual error measurement at the classifier-free guided output level to adjust decision boundaries online via an EMA feedback loop; and (3) momentum-augmented draft synthesis combining direction-magnitude gated residual extrapolation with anchor-guided unconditional correction. By transforming scheduling from a static risk accumulator into a feedback-driven, self-correcting controller, AlignCache consistently achieves superior acceleration-quality trade-offs across state-of-the-art video generation models. Our code is available at this https URL.

2610.16548.title: NoduleFlow: Automatic 3D Lung Nodule Detection and Segmentation
2610.16548.abstract: Low dose Computed Tomography (CT) is the standard imaging modality for lung cancer screening. On CT scans, lung cancer typically manifests as pulmonary nodules, whose manual identification is time-consuming and prone to observer variability, image quality limitations, and suboptimal reading conditions. Moreover, subtle temporal changes are often difficult to quantify reliably in CT scans from the same patient across follow-up examinations. Deep learning-based approaches for the automatic detection and segmentation of lung nodules have demonstrated improved accuracy and efficiency. However, most existing approaches provide only coarse region-of-interest localisation, rely on prior lesion annotations or human supervision, or treat detection and segmentation as separate tasks. In this work, we present NoduleFlow, a framework for lung nodule detection, classification, and segmentation directly from series of CT volumes. Our proposal consists of four interconnected modules and operates in an automated manner at inference time, without requiring prior lesion annotations, manual initialisation, or region-of-interest pre-selection. We further investigate whether nodule localization benefits from the propagation of candidate regions across follow-up scans through inter-scan registration fields, as opposed to conventional independent per-scan analysis. The generalisability of the framework is systematically evaluated across four independent datasets. The results underscore the potential of automated pipelines for lung nodule analysis in screening and diagnostic settings.

2610.16567.title: VLA-GAUGE: Systematically Evaluating Generalization and Robustness in Vision-Language-Action Models
2610.16567.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have achieved high success rates on familiar manipulation tasks, yet it remains unclear whether such scores reflect genuine zero-shot generalization and perturbation robustness. Existing evaluation frameworks provide limited capability-level diagnosis and combinatorial perturbation coverage, often without connecting diagnosis to targeted model refinement. We introduce VLA-GAUGE, a diagnostic framework that unifies both evaluations under a shared executable task representation. It combines (1) paired in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks across six capability suites, (2) single-factor sensitivity analysis with combinatorial perturbation screening and evaluation, and (3) diagnosis-driven refinement through targeted data augmentation and model fine-tuning. We evaluate 12 VLAs spanning different model sizes and action-modeling paradigms under a unified protocol. We find that (1) The mean Zero-Shot Score on VLA-GAUGE is only 22.3%, with SimpleVLA-RL scoring 8.0% and ranking second to last among the evaluated models. (2) Under three representative combinatorial perturbation configurations, the mean R-Score is 9.3. (3) Diagnosis-driven fine-tuning improves $\pi_{0.5}$'s zero-shot generalization and robustness under a selected perturbation combination on held-out scenarios by 72.4 and 31.8 scoring points, respectively; the latter exceeds the 10.9-point gain from LIBERO-Plus single-factor fine-tuning despite fewer successful training trajectories. These results show that high reported success rates on familiar manipulation tasks do not guarantee strong zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks or robustness to combinatorial perturbations, while diagnostic evaluation provides actionable signals for targeted model improvement.

2610.16570.title: Dense Endoluminal Mapping and Localisation from Monocular Bronchoscopy
2610.16570.abstract: Bronchoscopy inserts a camera through the airways to diagnose endoluminal disease. Locating the camera along the airway usually requires additional equipment, such as an electromagnetic tracker and a preoperative CT scan. In this paper, we investigate the use of the monocular camera stream to localise the bronchoscope without requiring additional sensing. We introduce a monocular SLAM system that localises the tip of a bronchoscope and reconstructs the airway surface around it from RGB video alone. A Depth Anything 3 backbone, fine-tuned on over a million photorealistic airway renderings, returns metric per-pixel depth and is the system's only source of scale. DINOv3 features routed through a custom cross-attention matcher supply sub-pixel correspondences on mucosa where classical descriptors fail. Both enter a factor graph alongside a dense constraint from projective iterative closest point (ICP) registration against the system's own running reconstruction, so surface evidence stabilises the directions the visual factors leave weakly observable. On six airways rendered from patient CT scans, the system reaches 26.1 mm mean absolute trajectory error and 77.5% mean surface F-score. Its mean surface accuracy exceeds that of five recent monocular SLAM and feed-forward baselines. MASt3R-SLAM, which fits a free scale to the ground truth, has a lower mean trajectory error (22.0 mm). ORB-SLAM3 completes only two of the six airways, whereas our system completes all six and also reconstructs two ex vivo specimens.

2610.16587.title: Code-Interactive Visual Reasoning for Financial Candlestick Understanding
2610.16587.abstract: Financial candlestick understanding requires locating visual elements, aligning them across trading dates and panels, and combining observations through numerical and financial reasoning. Answer accuracy alone does not reveal whether predictions are supported by chart evidence. We introduce Code-Interactive Financial Candlestick Reasoning and present Fin-Thinker, a model based on Qwen3.5-9B that generates and executes code to acquire evidence and perform computations. The model uses the returned observations to guide subsequent reasoning. To train these capabilities, we construct FinKLine-32K with 32,184 replay-verified code-observation trajectories collected through teacher-guided student exploration. These include successful solutions with and without error recovery. Our three-stage training framework combines foundational visual-code fine-tuning, financial process supervision of successful reasoning and corrective continuations, and execution-feedback reinforcement learning. For evaluation, we introduce FinKLineBench with 1,200 questions across 138 financial task types to assess answer correctness, code execution, and evidence grounding separately. On FinKLineBench, Fin-Thinker improves strict accuracy by 13.1 and 33.2 percentage points over the best-performing direct-answer baseline among those evaluated and its base model with sandbox access, respectively. Training-stage ablations further show that financial process supervision and execution-feedback reinforcement learning yield successive improvements in both answer accuracy and GPT-5.6-judged grounded accuracy.

2610.16591.title: JtT: Rethinking Point Trajectory Diffusion for Diverse and Rigid Motion from an Image
2610.16591.abstract: We study forecasting rigid-body motion from a single image: generating diverse and physically plausible future trajectories for arbitrary points in a scene, without building rigidity into the architecture or relying on geometric inputs such as depth. Like video generators, recent trajectory generators fail at this task, even in simple synthetic Kubric scenes, despite scaling up model size and training on real data. We show how to solve this with the right architecture and parameterization. Our model, JtT, is a simple diffusion transformer that operates directly in coordinate space and decodes arbitrary and dense query patterns, without the trajectory VAEs or fixed grids assumed in prior work. Through a systematic study of the design space of point trajectory diffusion, we find that diffusing per-frame velocities is the only parameterization that captures rigidity, that it must be paired with the right timestep schedule, and that adding full-resolution RGB at the query points resolves the boundary failures of prior methods. However, evaluating such 2D models rigorously is itself non-trivial. To our knowledge, we are the first to observe that physical plausibility and diversity do not improve together during training: larger models, as used in prior work, memorize the single ground-truth future per training image, becoming more rigid while covering fewer possible futures. Yet prior work has paid little attention to this, so we show how model rankings depend on model size, metric, and stopping time, and adopt a stricter, checkpoint-averaged evaluation protocol. Under this protocol, JtT improves over prior methods on both distributional and rigidity metrics and approaches ground-truth rigidity, with only about 50M parameters.

2610.16598.title: Detecting Chain-of-Thought Hijacking in Backdoored Multimodal Large Reasoning Models
2610.16598.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning enables multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs) to solve complex visual problems, but also exposes them to CoT hijacking: an adversary implants a backdoor through poisoned fine-tuning so that a visual trigger induces a hijacking turn, redirecting an otherwise faithful reasoning chain to an attacker-chosen answer. However, since the hijack acts within the reasoning chain, existing multimodal backdoor defenses designed for MLLMs that answer directly struggle to detect it. Moreover, inspecting the chain itself does not reliably expose the hijack, since the hijacking turn can resemble honest self-correction in form. In this paper, we find that honest reasoning tends to revise its answer at high-entropy "aha moments", whereas a hijack can overturn a confident answer through a near-deterministic turn. To quantify this contrast, we formalize this phenomenon as belief inertia, the cumulative next-token entropy of a reasoning span minus the answer-belief revision it induces, with markedly lower values for hijacked spans than for honest reasoning spans. Since hijacking tokens are also image-dependent, we further improve detection by restricting the measure to image-dependent spans, yielding visual belief inertia (VBI). Building on this, we propose InertiaGuard, a training-free, test-time detector that flags a trace when its VBI falls below a threshold calibrated on a small set of clean traces. Across various attacks and benchmarks, InertiaGuard achieves higher detection performance than existing baselines, while generalizing to different model architectures and trigger types.

2610.16622.title: Answer It or Not? Towards Prompt-Adapted Adversarial Images on Vision Language Models
2610.16622.abstract: With the advancement in language modeling, research on adversarial images has recently shifted from image classifiers to vision-language models (VLMs). Despite the new, text-prompt-driven nature of VLMs, we find that existing VLM adversaries have largely overlooked the dynamics of text prompts. In a typical use case, adversarial images can protect visual privacy by rejecting VLMs from answering questions about the image. However, existing protections are prompt-agnostic, i.e., indiscriminately rejecting any question, including those for potential legitimate use of the image. To address this limitation, we propose Prompt-Adapted (ProAda) adversarial images, which are optimized to balance the rejection of harmful prompts and the correct response of legitimate prompts. In particular, to achieve a more accurate adversarial direction, the text prompt is also iteratively updated with a simple classifier judging whether the harmfulness of the prompt remains. Extensive experiments on visual-privacy-related datasets validate that ProAda can reject over 90% of harmful prompts while allowing over 90% of legitimate ones, demonstrating superior overall performance compared to existing prompt-agnostic VLM adversaries. In addition, our ProAda achieves competitive overall cross-model transferability and improved robustness against countermeasures.

2610.16624.title: Adaptive Interaction Network for Human Motion Prediction During Human-Robot Collaboration
2610.16624.abstract: Human motion prediction during human-robot collaboration is critical for achieving safe and efficient interactions in shared environments. Unlike previous studies that have primarily focused on humans and objects, we focus on the robot-aware human motion prediction task, which explicitly models the influence of robots on human motion. This task presents new challenges, such as capturing human-robot heterogeneity and modeling complex spatial interactions. To address these issues, we develop an adaptive interaction network (AINet) model that consists of two branches: a primary branch that predicts future human motion and an auxiliary branch that estimates robot trajectories. The two branches are jointly optimized and coupled via a Local-Global Spatial Interaction (LGSI) Module, which effectively captures fine-grained and global contextual dependencies between human and robot motion sequences. Then, we introduce an Adaptive Weighted Aggregation (AWA) Module to dynamically fuse motion features using context-dependent weights, thereby increasing adaptability across diverse scenarios. Furthermore, we adopt a coarse-to-fine prediction strategy, in which a coarse pseudo-trajectory is first predicted, followed by the refinement of detailed human poses based on that trajectory. Extensive experiments on three challenging datasets reveal that our proposed method achieves superior performance, validating its effectiveness in human-robot collaboration scenarios. Our code is available at: this https URL.

2610.16632.title: REEL: Learning to Retrieve, Evaluate, and Evolve Visual Memory for Any Long-Horizon Multi-Shot Video Generation
2610.16632.abstract: Memory-based long-video generation aims to combine user control with long-range visual consistency. We organize this process into three functional components: a planner, an adapter, and a generator. Representative multi-shot systems couple memory to generator-specific interfaces or use predefined agent workflows, rather than independently training a memory policy for cross-shot objectives. We introduce REEL, a general-purpose visual-memory planner. Through a unified tool interface, REEL learns to retrieve references, create missing visual evidence, and update persistent memory. Backend-specific adapters translate its evidence plans into supported conditioning inputs, allowing the same policy to guide different black-box video generators. To train REEL, we construct two high-quality datasets, REEL-SFT-4k and REEL-RL-1k, covering diverse interaction patterns and prompt types. Training proceeds in three stages: supervised fine-tuning, single-shot Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), and multi-shot GRPO. Multi-shot GRPO carries policy-generated memory across consecutive shots, so later outcomes guide earlier reference selection and memory updates. REEL-Bench tests identity preservation and intended state changes under text-only requests and timed reference-image uploads. On JoyAI-Echo~1.5 and MiniMax-H3, REEL improves cross-shot consistency on ST-Bench by 15.1\% and 20.7\%, and Core-100 on our proposed REEL-Bench by 2.41 and 8.32 points, respectively, over the no-memory baseline.

2610.16666.title: Revisiting Natural Language Prompts from Large Language Models for Open-Vocabulary Video Recognition
2610.16666.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) like CLIP have shown great success in image tasks, however, applying CLIP to open-vocabulary video recognition poses challenges. Due to the limited text information, directly fine-tuning CLIP on video recognition datasets may lead to overfitting and hinder its generalizability. A prevalent method is to enrich text information by generating prompts using Large Language Models (LLMs). However, limited efforts have been made to explore how to generate higher-quality prompts that can contribute to classify unseen categories, and how to further enhance vision-text alignment based on these prompts. In this paper, we propose P2CLIP (Prompt-guided CLIP), which aims to bridge this gap by exploring the impact of prompts across three aspects: category, video, and frame. At the category level, we argue that LLM-generated prompts under simple instructions may suffer from semantic overgeneralization, which can blur the category boundaries and hinder the performance of the model. To address this issue, we design Generic-Discriminative Prompt using LLMs to obtain discriminative category embeddings with rich semantic information. At the video and frame levels, we first use VLM and LLM to generate frame and video descriptions for enhancing vision-text alignment. Then we propose a Knowledge-Guided Temporal Aggregation mechanism, which leverages the expert knowledge derived from LLMs to guide the temporal modeling of videos and encourage a better construction of the joint visual-textual feature space. Extensive experiments across various benchmarks, including zero-shot and few-shot settings, demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

2610.16679.title: EvoSpatial: Experience-Driven Skill and Tool Evolution for Spatial Reasoning Agents
2610.16679.abstract: Tool-augmented vision-language agents compose perception and measurement to reason about spatial relationships, but effective execution also requires tracking geometric assumptions and checking intermediate evidence. Preserving this experience across tasks requires retaining procedural knowledge together with the computations it governs. We introduce EvoSpatial, an experience-driven framework that evolves a library of linked skills and tools. Our key insight is that successful and failed spatial trajectories reveal both how to compute and when to trust the result. EvoSpatial retrieves skills, reuses tools, and synthesizes reusable computational functions (generated helpers) during reasoning. After answer submission, supervised outcome feedback guides skill refinement and tool consolidation for subsequent tasks. Across 20 benchmarks, EvoSpatial attains the highest average score among the compared spatial agents, exceeding SpatialClaw by 4.0 percentage points. Further experiments show cross-benchmark transfer and improved reasoning through skill-guided distillation without external skills at evaluation. These results support accumulating spatial experience for both inference-time reuse and trajectory-based training.

2610.16692.title: 3D-VITAL: Visibility-aware Identity Training from Artificial Liftings of 3D Reconstruction model for Cross-View Object Re-Identification
2610.16692.abstract: We address the Cross-View Object Re-Identification (ReID) task, aiming to match identities across drastically different viewpoints. We focus on Single-View Aerial-Ground ReID (SV AG-ReID), where models train on one viewpoint and must generalize to another at inference. To bridge this viewpoint gap, related work employs generative models to synthesize novel views from source images as additional training data. We leverage recent advances in large-scale single-view 3D mesh reconstruction to lift source images into textured meshes and to render them from new viewpoints. However, this pipeline produces unreliable data in two distinct ways. First, the reconstruction may fail and produce geometrically incorrect meshes, resulting in severe corruption in rendered novel views. Second, even when the geometry is correct, the rendered novel views contain hallucinated textures in regions not visible in the source image. The reconstructed mesh carries a per-pixel partition between regions visible from the source view and regions that the reconstruction model had to hallucinate, available as a deterministic byproduct of rendering. We introduce this per-pixel visibility map and exploit it in a two-stage design. Cross-View Consistency Filtering (CVCF) discards geometrically incorrect meshes by ensuring multi-view consistency between source and novel views over visible patches. Visibility-Aware Attention Supervision (VAAS) leverages the visibility map to guide the model's attention toward reliable regions of the rendered view during training. Combined, these two components enable our method, 3D-VITAL, to better leverage the synthetic signal from single-view 3D mesh reconstruction. 3D-VITAL sets a new state-of-the-art on three SV AG-ReID benchmarks. Code and data will be released at this https URL.

2610.16734.title: PathPilot: An Adaptive Question-Conditioned Multi-Magnification Navigation Agent for Whole-Slide Image Analysis
2610.16734.abstract: The diagnostic capability of WSI agents relies on effective slide navigation to identify diagnostically relevant regions and efficiently integrate evidence across the slide. While in clinical practice, pathologists dynamically examine slides across multiple scales, integrating global and cellular evidence in a sequential manner, existing AI navigation approaches mostly operate at a single fixed magnification or rely on predefined magnification traversal. This mismatch prevents existing methods from modeling cross-magnification interactions and adaptive magnification selection inherent to real diagnostic workflows. We propose PathPilot, a clinically consistent multi-magnification WSI navigation agent that explicitly models cross-magnification localization and evidence-adaptive exploration. Specifically, we introduce a CrossMagLoc that learns magnification-specific diagnostic localization from pathologist viewing behavior and integrates information from adjacent magnifications to identify the diagnostically most relevant region within the current ROI, thereby providing a diagnostically informed starting point for subsequent question-conditioned exploration. We further introduce an EviRegionSearch that starts question-conditioned exploration from this region, progressively accumulating question-relevant evidence and adaptively determining the next navigation action according to the remaining evidence requirement. Their iterative interaction enables PathPilot to sequentially explore across ROIs and magnifications until sufficient evidence is acquired. Extensive QA evaluations across five cohorts demonstrate consistent superiority over competing SOTA methods on inter/external cohorts, respectively, validating question-conditioned evidence acquisition across regions and magnifications that mirrors the sequential, knowledge-driven navigation of pathologists.

2610.16735.title: VAttnPO: Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization
2610.16735.abstract: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards commonly assigns one sequence advantage to an entire response. This outcome-level signal distinguishes overall response quality but leaves changes in visual-evidence use across generated tokens implicit. We introduce VAttnPO (Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization), which uses answer-conditioned visual attention to refine token-level credit while preserving the verifier-derived trajectory-mean advantage. A frozen old policy constructs a visual reference by teacher forcing the known correct answer and produces a visual distribution for each rollout token. VAttnPO measures their agreement in visual-attention space using Jensen--Shannon divergence, rather than reading guidance from teacher output-token distributions or introducing an attention-matching objective. Trajectory centering, relative-position weighting, and credit balancing turn this agreement into a zero-mean, position-aware correction to the GRPO sequence advantage. Token intervention, visual-index permutation, and trajectory analysis provide diagnostic evidence linking this signal to model behavior, visual correspondence, and generation position. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, VAttnPO raises six-task image AVE from 70.97 with GRPO to 73.50 and scores higher on every reported structured, video, and MME metric. Gains over GRPO also hold on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL3-8B-Instruct.

2610.16744.title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
2610.16744.abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

2610.16749.title: The Midas Touch for Metric Depth: Interpretable Metricization for Generalizable Depth Perception
2610.16749.abstract: Recent foundation models have drastically improved the generalization of monocular relative depth estimation, yet recovering accurate metric depth from their estimates for depth perception tasks remains challenging due to scale ambiguity and local metric-scale inconsistency. Existing approaches recover metric depth from sparse observations using either explicit global affine transformation algorithms or implicit data-driven depth completion networks. The former cannot accommodate spatially varying relative-to-metric relationships, while the latter are sensitive to the distribution of sparse observations and may not fully exploit generalizable relative depth priors. To simultaneously address these issues, this study extends our previous work MTD and proposes MTDv2, a hybrid metric depth perception framework that combines explicit depth metricization with data-driven metric depth refinement. The explicit depth metricization process performs segment-wise affine transformations to recover spatially varying metric scales while preserving the geometric structure of relative depth, followed by pixel-wise depth refinement that propagates metric observations along paths with minimal accumulated geometric variation. The data-driven depth refinement process subsequently extends the explicit single-path depth propagation to a learnable multi-path formulation while preserving its interpretability. Extensive experiments conducted on 16 public datasets demonstrate the robust and generalizable depth scale recovery capability of MTDv2 across diverse sources of sparse observations and different depth estimation paradigms, as well as its broad applicability to downstream 3D perception tasks. Code will be publicly available at this https URL upon publication.

2610.16759.title: Image Tokenizers Should Be Trained Between Images
2610.16759.abstract: Latent diffusion models generate images as codes of an image tokenizer, whose decoder turns them into the pixel image. Recent tokenizers improve how well these codes reconstruct an image and how easily a generator learns them. Yet a generator does not reproduce the codes of training images, and when a generated code lands outside what the decoder expects, the decoded image contains imperfections. Current methods make the decoder more robust to generated codes by adding noise during training. However, generated codes lie between the training codes and resemble their mixture more than one of them plus noise. To improve generated images, decoders should therefore be trained on codes in the space between training samples. We propose InterpTok, which fine-tunes MAETok to decode mixtures of image codes into natural images. Since no target image exists between two training samples, a discriminator judges whether each decoded mixture looks as natural as its two sources. A mixing ratio loss requires the decoded mixture to keep the mixing ratio of the two codes. Together, they prevent collapse to a trivial solution and yield a sharp and natural composition of both images. InterpTok keeps MAETok's reconstruction quality and improves interpolation quality more than threefold, the best of all tokenizers in a recent benchmark. Beyond interpolation, InterpTok improves the generation FID of a matched diffusion transformer from 11.61 to 8.48 without guidance, and even reaches 8.11 at an eighth of the sampling steps, where the generator on MAETok's codes worsens. The generator trained on our tokenizer also reaches the final result of the one trained on MAETok at half the training steps. Our findings show that the space between image codes can and should be explicitly supervised rather than ignored.

2610.16762.title: Towards Complementary Keypoint Detection via Mixture of Detectors
2610.16762.abstract: Keypoint detection plays a central role in geometric vision pipelines. Existing detectors exhibit complementary strengths across different scene structures and keypoint budgets, and reliance on a single detector often results in suboptimal keypoint distributions. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Mixture of Detectors (MoD)} for dense matching pipelines, a unified framework for complementary keypoint detection through the adaptive composition of heterogeneous detectors. MoD first distills heterogeneous detectors into a unified model, allowing diverse detection maps to be predicted efficiently within a single forward pass.
